notes: POC focused on on-prem air-gapped IDE copilot. Customer wants native JetBrains + VS Code plugins with LSP streaming support. Emphasis on low token latency for completions (<60ms p95), smooth character-by-character streaming in-editor, and deterministic model pinning per workspace. Security: full audit logs, signed offline model bundles, KMS/HSM for key wrapping, strict retention policies. Legal asked about third-party model license (no weights can be redistributed unless explicitly allowed) — impacts offline update mechanism. Team expressed willingness to accept quantized 4-bit models if output parity is good. UX ask: rolling model upgrades with quick rollback button in Console. Conversation snippets: "We cannot phone home for fallback models"; "Need a signed tarball process we can load via airgap USB or internal registry". Budget oriented to reserved capacity if packaging moves to production.

requirements_summary: Primary workload: IDE copilot & code completion with streaming token output. Targets: 50 concurrent streaming sessions, p95 token latency <60ms, cold-start for model shard <200ms, support for 200 active developers, ~150k tokens/day. Model policy: pin model per-team, allow exact version rollback, and deterministic fallback to a smaller quantized model when memory constrained. Offline updates must be delivered as signed, integrity-checked tarballs; update process must work over airgap via USB or internal package registry. Packaging: OCI-compatible bundles, minimal runtime footprint, local metrics exporters that push to internal Prometheus (no external telemetry). Hardware: guidance requested for 8-16 GPU equivalent. Networking: 100GbE inside cluster, separate mgmt VLAN for update ingestion. Storage: fast NVMe for KV caches and 2TB storage per node for model shards.
poc_scope: 30-day POC: demonstrate low-latency streaming in VS Code & IntelliJ, validate model pinning and rollback, prove offline update flow using signed bundle, measure latency/throughput and cost estimate for Dedicated/Private. Success criteria: p95 token latency <60ms, 95% of completions within expected relevance delta vs hosted model, secure offline update completed without internet egress.
hardware_request: Initial sizing recommendation provided by Redwood SE: baseline for 50 concurrent streams = 4x H100 80GB GPUs (distributed across 2 nodes, 2 GPUs each) for headroom; alternative cost-optimized config: 4x A100 80GB across 2 nodes with aggressive quantization (4-bit) and batching. Additional reqs: 2TB NVMe per node, 1TB swap for KV cache, 100Gbps intra-node network, airgap-friendly image registry, 1 rack PDUs and cold-storage for signed bundles.
procurement_notes: ZenForge procurement prefers cloud reseller quotes for on-prem H100 racks or bundled appliance. They asked for a line-item cost for Reserved Dedicated vs Private license + support. Procurement timeline: internal budget review in March, purchase order earliest April if POC goes well.
